# Petabyte-Scale Legacy-to-AWS: A Serverless Lakehouse You Can Actually Run

## Land decades of history + CDC from Oracle/SQL Server/etc. into S3, secure it with tags & LF-tags, query with Athena/Iceberg, add full-text search, and train ML — all serverlessly and cost-optimized.

Reading time: 12–15 mins Audience: Senior/Principal Data & ML Architects, Platform Engineering, FinOps

This blueprint shows how to migrate petabyte-scale historical + CDC data from common legacy databases into an AWS serverless lakehouse on Amazon S3. You’ll use object tags and Lake Formation LF-tags for governance and automated lifecycle (Intelligent-Tiering/Glacier), Athena + Iceberg for ACID/time-travel queries, OpenSearch Serverless for free-text search, and Step Functions + SageMaker to train ML on ephemeral compute. Code samples include CDK (TypeScript), PySpark (Glue), SQL (Athena), Lambda (Node.js), and SageMaker SDK (Python).

This post gives you the reference architecture + deploy-ready snippets to make it real.

## The usual legacy suspects & migration patterns

Most migrations involve Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Db2, Teradata, Netezza; on the doc side MongoDB is common.

Patterns that work

## S3 with tags, lifecycle, (optional) replication — CDK (TypeScript)

Why tags? S3 object tags (up to 10 per object) let you target lifecycle transitions/expirations per dataset. Combine with Intelligent-Tiering for hands-off cost optimization.

When to use: operational search, log/event exploration, schema-less discovery, data portal search.

Tip: Use a search collection, encryption policy, and a scoped data-access policy. No domain sizing, no nodes.

Legacy system Landing & CDC Lakehouse & Query Notes Oracle DMS full+CDC → S3 Parquet Athena + Iceberg + LF-tags Use SCT later if moving to Aurora PG. SQL Server DMS → S3 Parquet Same as above Great serverless analytics candidate.
